Based on my research, there appears to be some confusion in your question between two different record-holding cats owned by Jake Perry in Austin, Texas:

1. **Creme Puff** - The **oldest cat ever recorded** (Guinness World Record holder at 38 years and 3 days, living from August 3, 1967 to August 6, 2005). However, she **never received the Cat of the Year award**.

2. **Grandpa (Granpa Rexs Allen)** - Received the **1999 Cat of the Year** award posthumously from *Cats & Kittens* magazine when he died in 1998 at age 34 years and 2 months. While exceptionally old, he was not the oldest cat ever recorded.

So to directly answer your question: The oldest cat ever recorded (**Creme Puff**) did **not** receive the Cat of the Year award. If you're asking about which cat received the Cat of the Year award, that was **Grandpa in 1999**, though he wasn't technically the oldest cat ever recorded.

There may be some conflation in popular stories between these two cats, as they were both famous longevity champions from the same owner in Texas.
